sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Bergen op Zoom charges for street parking in seven zones, from the core inside the old ramparts to the hospital streets. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 13 November 2025, with the levy from 1 January 2026. In zone A, the core, it costs 2.70 euros for the first two hours and then 5.00 euros an hour. Zone B, around Mineurplein and the Korenmarkt, costs 2.10 euros an hour with a day card of 13.50 euros, and zone C, the ring around the core, 2.00 euros an hour or 9.00 euros a day [0]. Plein XIII and the harbour cost 1.50 euros an hour, the streets next to Lievensberg hospital 1.10 euros, the area around Bravis hospital 12.00 euros a day only, and the camper spaces on the Boulevard 10.00 euros a night [1]. A first resident permit costs 53.40 to 71.40 euros a year, depending on the zone, and a second 79.20 to 261.00 euros; business permits cost 397.20 to 523.80 euros [2]. The fine is 82.00 euros, wheel-clamp removal 168.65 euros and no remission is granted [3]. The payment hours are set by a separate college decision of 2022, which gives 9:00 to 21:00 Monday to Saturday in the core and 9:00 to 18:30 in zone C, but the register still shows it as valid and its zone-A tariff structure differs from the 2026 ordinance, so the current hours are unverified [17]. In April 2025 the executive announced that four older documents of 2012 to 2015 would be replaced by a new mobility note for 2025 to 2035 and a new parking-standards note, with a neighbourhood approach based on a parking survey [9]. In December 2025 two motions were tabled, one to resubmit the parking-norms note in the second quarter of 2026 and one to study abolishing paid parking for low-income disabled card holders; we did not read the votes [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The centre's garage question is the story. The De Parade garage is in a building with several owners, and a council memo of October 2025 says it is little used because of poor access and limited social control, with falling occupancy, nuisance and vacant shops around it, but gives no occupancy figures [4][5]. The proposal to refurbish it, with a widened car entrance, open stairs and a lockable entrance on Sint-Josephstraat, is costed at 2.58 million euros, with 1.0 million from a national subsidy and 1.24 million municipal; this is a proposal, and the memo says the estimate carries a 20 percent margin [6]. According to an entrepreneurs' association, not a council document, the council discussed the investment on 10 March 2026 and made financing available, with works planned for 2027, and we read no amount or decision [14]. The 2022 concept vision for the inner city wants visitors to park in the garages and as little as possible on the street, with garages becoming parking hubs and an area near Mineurplein as search area for a new hub; it also says visitors like the two city-centre garages less than the squares [12][13]. On charging, a traffic decision of 16 July 2026 designates charging spaces at seven locations in Bergen op Zoom and Halsteren [15], and a decision of 26 June 2026 reserves spaces for a three-year Greenwheels shared-car pilot [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text: We found no source on who operates the garages or the park-and-ride, and no occupancy figures, because the municipal site was offline when we read it. Our data cover the P+R at Parallelweg, with 126 spaces, for about 54 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 18% on weekdays and 7% at weekends, with a peak of 69% around midday on a Tuesday. The garages and street parking are not in our data.
